A premenopausal or postmenopausal woman presents with insidious-onset shortness of breath and fatigue. No red-flag associated symptoms (e.g., chest pain, fever, hemoptysis, orthopnea, edema) or risk factors (e.g., smoking, heart/lung disease, anemia) are identified.

The clinical presentation centers on a woman (pre- or postmenopausal) with insidious dyspnea and fatigue — nonspecific but concerning for systemic or volume-overload pathology. - Absence of risk factors for alternative diagnoses (no smoking, no known heart/lung disease, no anemia, no immunosuppression)  
- Normal CBC (WBC, Hgb, platelets within limits) — argues against infection, inflammation, or marrow infiltration  

[GAPS]  
- Pleural fluid cytology — required to confirm malignant cells  
- Ascitic fluid cytology — critical to establish peritoneal carcinomatosis  
- Serum CA-125 level — highly sensitive for epithelial ovarian cancer, especially HGSC  
- Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen/pelvis — needed to assess tumor burden, lymphadenopathy, omental involvement, and hepatic metastases  
- Transvaginal ultrasound — higher-resolution characterization of ovarian mass morphology (e.g., solid components, papillary projections, vascularity)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma
